mainEntity.name: Why do dentists recommend check-ups every six months?

acceptedAnswer.text: The six-month interval is a widely recommended guideline that suits most patients, as it allows dentists to monitor oral health changes and catch potential problems early. However, the ideal frequency may vary depending on individual risk factors such as gum health, history of decay, or medical conditions. Your dentist will advise on the most appropriate recall interval for your specific circumstances following a clinical assessment. Some patients may benefit from more frequent visits, while others with consistently good oral health may be advised that longer intervals are appropriate.

mainEntity.name: What if I have no pain — do I still need a dental check-up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and this is one of the most important points to understand. Many dental conditions, including early-stage decay and gum disease, are painless in their initial stages. By the time pain develops, the condition may have progressed significantly, potentially requiring more complex treatment. A routine dental examination can identify issues that you may not be aware of, allowing for earlier intervention. Attending regular check-ups even when you feel well is a proactive approach to maintaining your dental health and avoiding preventable problems.

mainEntity.name: How much does a dental examination cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of a dental examination can vary depending on the practice and whether additional investigations such as X-rays are required. At a private dental practice, examination fees are typically straightforward. Your dental practice can provide a clear breakdown of costs before your appointment, as fees may vary depending on individual treatment needs and any additional investigations required. Many patients find that the investment in regular preventative care is considerably less than the cost of managing advanced dental conditions.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a dental check-up and a hygiene appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dental check-up involves a comprehensive assessment of your oral health by a dentist, including screening for decay, gum disease, oral cancer, and other conditions. A hygiene appointment focuses on professional cleaning to remove plaque and tartar build-up, along with personalised oral hygiene advice. Both are important components of a thorough dental care routine, and they complement each other effectively. Your dentist may recommend both at intervals suited to your individual needs.

mainEntity.name: Can dental check-ups really help prevent serious problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular dental examinations significantly support the early identification of potential issues, which in many cases allows for less invasive management. Conditions such as gum disease, when identified and managed early, can often be stabilised to prevent progression. Similarly, early detection of unusual soft tissue changes during oral cancer screening can be critically important. While no healthcare approach can guarantee the prevention of all conditions, consistent professional monitoring is one of the most reliable strategies for protecting your long-term oral health.

mainEntity.name: I haven't been to the dentist in years — is it too late to start again?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is never too late to re-engage with dental care. Dentists understand that many people experience gaps in their dental attendance for various reasons, and a good dental practice will provide a welcoming, non-judgemental environment. Your first appointment back will typically involve a thorough assessment of your current oral health, and your dentist will discuss any findings with you clearly and calmly. A personalised plan can then be developed to address any concerns and establish a routine that supports your ongoing oral health.
